name: brick
tagline: Server-rendered HTML components for Go, on html/template
description: A component-based HTML render engine for Go built on html/template: pages, layouts and components are .html files, components are tags, and brick adds a calling convention, never a new template language. It grows into a full site layer, islands, server actions and bindings without a client framework, and ships a 133-component UI kit.

positioning.category: Go HTML templating and server-rendered UI
positioning.audience: Go developers building server-rendered websites and web apps who want components without a JavaScript framework or a build step
positioning.wedge: Go's html/template has no components: every reusable piece of markup is a copy-pasted define block. brick makes a component a file and a tag, keeps html/template's escaping, and adds interactivity from the server, so a Go app gets a component UI with no bundler and no new template language.
differentiators: Components are .html files and tags (<Card> or <x-card>) with props, children, named and scoped slots, and context
Every {{ }} is Go's own html/template, so escaping and the whole template language are unchanged
No build step and no code generation: drop a file, it is a component
Server-side interactivity: islands, server actions, two-way bindings and in-place navigation from a small runtime (about 5 KB gzipped, plus 3 KB for navigation)
A site layer with routes, markdown pages, collections, a render cache, live reload, static export and sub-path hosting
Scripts are sandboxed Starlark; every file path is confined to the project
A 133-component UI kit that works without JavaScript and gets better with it, with twelve demo apps
